Get seed table annotations for root IDs

octo_annotations.Rd

Looks up the SeaTable annotations of neurons by root ID. The result has one row per input ID, in the same order (duplicates kept), so it can be added directly to another table, e.g. synapse counts.

Usage

octo_annotations(
  ids,
  columns = c("cell_type", "group", "soma_side", "seymour_match_id"),
  all = FALSE,
  table = getOption("octor.seatable_table"),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

ids

root IDs (character)

columns

seed table columns to return. NULL returns all columns.

all

return all matching rows (with the SeaTable row id _id) instead of one row per input ID

table

SeaTable table name

refresh

read the table again instead of using the cached copy

Value

data.frame with root_id, the requested columns (as text), and n_rows: how many seed rows share this root ID (0 if not found)

Details

When several rows share a root ID (a neuron seeded more than once), the trusted row is used: primary / primary (auto) / unique first, then conflicting rows, then secondary ones (see octo_update_ids()). Use all = TRUE to get every matching row instead.

IDs not found in the table get NA. That usually means the neuron has no seed yet, or the ID is outdated: run octo_update_ids() to refresh the table, or octo_latestid() to update your IDs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ann <- octo_annotations(pre_counts$rootid_pre, c("cell_type", "soma_side"))
pre_counts <- cbind(pre_counts, ann[, -1])

octo_annotations("720575940...", columns = NULL)            # everything
octo_annotations(ids, "cell_type", all = TRUE)              # all seed rows
} # }
